sections.h2: Where is Coon Rapids and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Coon Rapids is a northern suburb of Minneapolis and the second-largest city in Anoka County. It holds 22.61 square miles of land at about 863 feet above sea level, and the Census Bureau estimates 64,193 residents as of July 1, 2025.

The Mississippi River runs along the city, and Cenaiko Lake and Crooked Lake sit inside the boundaries. Two-thirds of Crooked Lake is in Coon Rapids and the rest is in Andover. U.S. Highway 10, Minnesota Highway 47 and Minnesota Highway 610 carry most of the traffic, and the BNSF mainline cuts through town. Coon Rapids Boulevard, which follows the old oxcart route, is still the main commercial corridor. A house a block from those roads draws different buyers than one on a quiet street near a park, so the address shapes how a sale goes.

sections.h2: How did Coon Rapids grow into a city of about 64,000?
sections.html:
Coon Rapids began around Coon Creek, named for the raccoons hunted at its mouth in the 1800s. The Red River Ox Cart Trail was laid out in 1835 to link Minneapolis and Anoka, and the first industries grew up along it. One was the Anoka Pressed Brick and Terra Cotta Company, started by D. C. Dunham in 1881. Its clay pit, still called the Clay Hole, is a local landmark.

Work on the Coon Rapids Dam began in 1912 and finished in 1914, and the dam marks the northernmost navigable point on the Mississippi. The Hennepin County Park Board bought it in 1969, and it is now part of Coon Rapids Dam Regional Park. The place incorporated as a village in October 1952 and as a city in June 1959.

Growth after that was fast. The count was 14,931 in 1960, 30,505 in 1970, 52,978 in 1990 and 63,599 at the 2020 census. A city that more than tripled between 1960 and 1990 has many houses that are now several decades old, which is worth remembering when you think about roofs, windows and mechanical systems before listing.

sections.h2: What jobs, schools and parks affect home values in Coon Rapids?
sections.html:
Health care, schools and manufacturing anchor the local job base. The city's 2014 financial report listed its largest employers, and the list below shows the top of it.

  • Mercy Health, part of Allina Health, with 1,860 employees.
  • Independent School District 11, with 1,238.
  • Mary T, Inc., a health care and housing provider, with 1,120.
  • RMS Company, a medical device maker, with 672, followed by Honeywell Aerospace with 600 and Anoka-Ramsey Community College with 403.

Public schools belong to the Anoka-Hennepin School District. Coon Rapids High School is projected at about 1,935 students for 2025-26, and the middle schools are Coon Rapids Middle and Northdale Middle. The seven elementary schools are Adams, Eisenhower, Hamilton, Hoover, Mississippi, Morris Bye and Sand Creek. Charter options include Paladin Career and Technical High School and Northwest Passage High School.

For recreation, Bunker Hills Regional Park, with its Bunker Beach water park, and Coon Rapids Dam Regional Park are both regional parks inside the city limits.

sections.html:

sections.h2: Which Coon Rapids rental and vacancy rules matter when you sell?
sections.html:
Coon Rapids regulates rentals and empty houses more closely than many suburbs, and the rules can affect both your timeline and what a buyer will do with the property.

  • Every rental, single-family homes included, must hold a city license before tenants move in. Processing takes about 4 to 6 weeks and includes a background check for each owner, a training certificate and a passed inspection.
  • Licenses renew every year, and starting in 2026 a late renewal brings a late fee. Inspections run on a 1, 2 or 3 year cycle based on results.
  • Airbnb, Vrbo and other short-term rentals are prohibited under City Code 12-904, so a buyer cannot plan on that use.
  • A vacant house needs a vacant property permit. You submit the application with the fee, then call Building Inspections at 763-767-6476 to book a one-hour inspection.

If tenants live in the house, call the Housing Inspector at 763-767-6575 before you list. That call tells you where your license and inspection cycle stand.

sections.h2: Do repairs before a Coon Rapids sale need permits?
sections.html:
Yes, most of them do. The city says building permits are needed for windows, siding, roofing, electrical and plumbing work, drywall, demolition, framing, additions, garages, driveways, steps and decks, and licensed contractors may be required for some jobs.

A fix made without a permit can surface later when a buyer's inspector asks about it. Call the Inspections Division at 763-767-6476 before you hire anyone. If the house needs more work than you want to take on, selling as-is to a buyer who handles repairs after closing is a common alternative, though the price will reflect that.

sections.h2: What does Anoka County require to record a Coon Rapids deed?
sections.html:
The Anoka County Recorder accepts the deed for filing. State deed tax is 0.33 percent of net consideration under Minnesota Statutes 287.21. At the Census median value of $305,800 that works out to roughly $1,009.

  • The deed tax is $1.65 when the price is $3,000 or less.
  • An agricultural conservation fee of $5 applies to transfer documents.
  • A completed electronic Certificate of Real Estate Value and its number go on the deed when required.
  • The deed must say where to send tax statements, with the buyer's name and address.
  • Delinquent taxes must be paid in full before recording.
  • A well disclosure certificate with a $54 fee, or the approved well statement on the deed, is required.

Most Anoka County property is abstract property, so the county advises a thorough title search before a sale. Recording questions go to 763-323-5400 at the Government Center in Anoka. Minnesota Statutes 513.55 separately requires you to give the buyer a written disclosure of material facts you know about before you sign.

sections.h2: How is property tax paid when a Coon Rapids house sells?
sections.html:
Anoka County Property Records and Taxation collects the tax, and you can look up what is owed by parcel number or address at the county's property access site. Ask the county at 763-323-5400 for the unpaid balance and the next due date, and ask the title company how the year's tax is split at closing.

Payment options matter if you still owe tax before the sale. Online payment through PayAnokaCounty carries a 2.6 percent fee for cards and Apple or Google Pay and a $3.50 fee for eCheck. Checks by mail must be postmarked on or before the due date, and paper checks paid in person at the Government Center, open 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, carry no fee. The county's free Direct Payment Program pulls the amount from a bank account on the due date.

sections.h2: What are your choices for selling a house in Coon Rapids?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell it yourself, or accept an offer from a cash buyer, and the right route depends on the condition of the house and how soon you need to close.

A listing usually brings the widest pool of buyers and works best for a house in solid shape. A direct cash sale trades some price for speed and fewer conditions, and it can suit a vacant house, a former rental that needs inspection work, or a property with deferred repairs. Whatever you choose, gather the rental license status, any open permits, the well disclosure and the tax balance first, because every buyer will ask for them.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Coon Rapids house that has tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes, but check your rental license first. Coon Rapids requires every rental, including single-family homes, to be licensed and inspected, so call the Housing Inspector at 763-767-6575 to confirm where your license and inspection cycle stand before you list or accept an offer.

faqs.q: Can a buyer run a short-term rental in a Coon Rapids house?
faqs.a: No. City Code 12-904 prohibits Airbnb, Vrbo and other short-term rentals in Coon Rapids, so a buyer who plans that use cannot rely on it.

faqs.q: How much is the state deed tax on a Coon Rapids sale?
faqs.a: The tax is 0.33 percent of net consideration, or $1.65 when the price is $3,000 or less. On a $305,800 sale, the Census median value for the city, that is about $1,009. Anoka County adds a $5 conservation fee, and a well disclosure certificate costs $54 unless the approved well statement appears on the deed.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit before fixing up my Coon Rapids house to sell?
faqs.a: For most projects, yes. Windows, siding, roofing, electrical, plumbing, drywall, decks, driveways and additions all need building permits. Call the Inspections Division at 763-767-6476 if you are unsure.

faqs.q: What happens with a vacant house in Coon Rapids?
faqs.a: A vacant house needs a vacant property permit. Submit the application and fee at City Hall, then call Building Inspections at 763-767-6476 to schedule the one-hour inspection. Property Maintenance at 763-767-6470 handles complaints about empty properties.
